INTERVIEW SUMMARY
Matt believes that to exceed a customer's expectations, it all comes down to customer service.
He will always try to anticipate their needs before they have to ask. He prides himself in helping
crewmembers out. As a Training Officer, he will break the ice with a smile. He does a lot of
mentoring with new crewmembers. With clients, it is a smile and a firm handshake. He
believes there is a fine line between professional and personal. He will make small talk with the
client and perhaps ask about the weekend, but he always keeps it professional.
He is a planner for contingencies and multiple contingencies. He feels Corporate Aviation is all
about change and being ready. He uses clear and concise verbiage. Regarding confidential
information, he does not disclose anything. When talking to friends, he will keep all of his
information vague.
Matt is honest and upfront. Trust is extremely important to him. Teamwork, in his mind, is what
gets a trip done. He is a very detail oriented and good employee who is service oriented, loyal,
dedicated and committed to his job.
Matt feels he is the airport kid. His aviation career began twenty-two years ago sweeping
hanger floors and washing airplanes. Within a couple years, he was driving an airport fuel truck.
At twenty-one, he secured a position at FlightSafety International as a Simulator Co-Pilot. That
was a tremendous opportunity. His time at FlightSafety gave him a good look at various
departments, and he was able to learn what worked and what did not. A full-time position flying
as a Co-Pilot on a Hawker followed. By thirty, he secured a Co-Pilot position on a Gulfstream.
A Captain's position came in due course. At forty, he is now an Entry-level Manager and Lead
Captain flying an ultra-long range G-550. It has been a long ride, with many sacrifices but well
worth the effort.
When thinking of a change, Matt feels working for individuals versus a traditional corporate flight
department provides unique challenges often with a very personalized approach to service.
While working for an individual many years ago, he found meeting the principal's requests
beyond the normal pilot duties, provided him with a sense of completion and satisfaction not
typically experienced with a traditional corporate department. He would enjoy that again. He is
ready for a new challenge.
In his free time, he enjoys restoring antique farm equipment and works and manages a small
hobby farm. He also likes outdoor sports and spending time with his family.
